clue.text: Having ground for lawsuit, arranged bail at once

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put into a new order, so these words get reshuffled

explanation.surface: A lawyer notes that bail has been sorted out at once, giving grounds to sue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the ten letters of BAIL AT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter giving legal grounds for a lawsuit is described in law as one on which action can be taken.

indicators.note: something done repeatedly happens more than once, so the word is given twice

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying to show they approve.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled cry is the traditional shout of agreement in the British House of Commons.

clue.text: Close in an attempt to be fashionable

indicators.note: one word is placed in the other, so the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: an attempt is a try
a close is an end or conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone tries hard to keep up with fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like an adjective meaning near, but it is the noun meaning end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up to date with the latest style is a synonym for fashionable.

clue.text: A stake in a buoyant economy

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: An investor puts money into a booming economy.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the stake each player puts in before the deal is called this.

parts.note: read as something that matches a shape exactly, like a garment cut to the body

explanation.surface: Something conforms precisely to the expected pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment or part that matches the required shape precisely is said to be ideally fitted.

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a lemon tastes oddly sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk pudding made from wheat grains is a British sweet, the word for a dessert course.

clue.text: The way to the Circle Line

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a circle is a ring

explanation.surface: Directions to the Circle Line on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground line, but here 'Circle' and 'Line' are separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of cord or twine is a line.

definitions.meaning: an American slang word for a military prison or jail

explanation.surface: An American prison ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an American military lock-up and a two-masted sailing vessel.

parts.note: read not as a guest bedroom but as the spare space or headroom left between things

explanation.surface: Talk of the guest bedroom in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The free space allowed between two objects, as under a bridge, is called this.

clue.text: Go in for chips without fish

definitions.text: Go in for chips without fish

parts.words: Go in for chips without fish
parts.note: read as walking into a chip shop to buy chips alone

explanation.surface: Ordering chips at the chippy with no fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rufus cryptic definition: you go in to a chip shop for chips, and 'go in' is the sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a place is a plain synonym of the verb, as in going through a door.

clue.text: When guns are effectively fired in anger, perhaps

indicators.note: fired suggests being set off or worked up, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Guns are let off in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' rearranges IN ANGER; 'perhaps' marks the surface as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns can hit a target only when it lies within their reach, the distance they can cover.

clue.text: Running easily for victory in the return game

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so the victory sits inside
a return goes back, so the game's name is read backwards

parts.note: golf is a game
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A team cruises to victory in the return match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the game round to FLOG; 'in' then houses the victory. 'the return game' reads as a rematch, which is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving smoothly and easily, as a stream or prose does, is a synonym.

parts.note: read not as greedy people but as people who lack a great deal

explanation.surface: A remark about demanding, greedy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor people lacking the necessities of life are described with this adjective.

definitions.meaning: collecting things up from the ground
improving, as trade does after a slump

explanation.surface: A firm that collects things finds its trade improving.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both lifting or collecting things and recovering or improving.

parts.note: to blow is to puff
adders are those that compute, adding up figures

explanation.surface: Someone curses their computers for being dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: These venomous African snakes are among the deadliest in the world.

clue.text: It's present in a constantly recurring form

indicators.note: a new form means a new shape, so the letters take a different order

explanation.surface: Something that is here now comes back again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a ... form' rearranges the ten letters of IT'S PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps coming back or continues stubbornly is described with this adjective.

parts.note: read not as acting shamefaced but as acting like sheep in a flock, keeping together as the proverb says

explanation.surface: People who are embarrassed behave awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says these 'flock together', which is what sheep do.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says those alike in kind flock together, like sheep.

clue.text: Taking one drink laced with another

indicators.note: lacing a drink means slipping something into it, so one drink goes inside the other

parts.note: a sling is a drink of spirit, sugar and water, as in gin sling
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink spiked with something else is taken.
explanation.walkthrough: A sling is a cocktail of spirit, sugar and water; 'laced with' places the tea within it. 'Taking' is the definition, in the sense of thieving.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking what belongs to someone else without permission is theft.

parts.note: read as a servant who works with her hands, playing on manual meaning of the hand

explanation.surface: A labourer doing low manual work.
explanation.definitionFit: A female servant or attendant is an old word for such a menial.

clue.text: Possibly untax beer, but spirits remain high

definitions.note: a clause describing a state, standing for the adjective

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: If beer were tax-free drinkers would stay cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges UNTAX BEER; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of energy and cheerfulness is in high spirits.

clue.text: A ragged child may be an old city feature

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city in Mesopotamia
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A scruffy child is part of the scenery of an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous, poorly dressed child is a common sense of this word.

clue.text: Deserted area is in a bad way

indicators.note: in a bad way means disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula between Egypt and Israel is largely desert.

definitions.meaning: to decide or sort out a matter

explanation.surface: Someone decides to clear what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to decide a dispute and to pay off a bill.

definitions.meaning: secured with a clasp, as a belt is

explanation.surface: Something tied tight then collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both fastening a strap with a clasp and crumpling under strain.

definitions.meaning: a stream, something that flows, in northern English dialect
a nod or signal of command, as in at someone's call

explanation.surface: A graceful sweep of the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In northern England a small stream is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a brook in northern England and a summoning gesture, as in beck and call.

parts.note: to tempt is an old sense of to test or try, as in tempting fate

explanation.surface: Having a go at an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a shot at something is making a try at it.

clue.text: A pound's put on for services

definitions.note: a description of garments, standing for a plural noun

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight, here plural

explanation.surface: A pound is added to the cost of the services.
explanation.definitionFit: These white linen vestments are worn by clergy at church services.

indicators.note: read as gorm-less, the syllable gorm removed from the word

parts.note: Cairngorm is a mountain in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A stupid hill-walking dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gormless' (British for stupid) is split as 'Gorm-less': take GORM from CAIRNGORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rough-coated Scottish terrier is named after the Highland stone mounds.

parts.note: a rebel is one who is defiant
a lion is a beast

explanation.surface: A defiant animal stands up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is a revolt against authority.
